# Stephen Umunna

> AdTech operations and engineering executive. Builder-operator hybrid: CTO/Acting COO at Confidential AdTech Startup (built two-sided AdTech platform with 21M-profile CDP and 100x consumer growth). Senior Account Operations Manager at Causal IQ (managed up to $1.2M/month across 6 DSPs for major brand clients including CDC, Hertz, Grammarly, Orangetheory). Educational platform built for Stanford's BIOE 230 course in 24 hours with Claude Code + Vercel AI SDK + Gemini.

## Roles
- Chief Technology Officer / Acting Chief Operating Officer at Confidential AdTech Startup (Apr 2025 - Mar 2026)
- Senior Account Operations Manager at Causal IQ (Nov 2022 - Mar 2025)
- Account Operations Manager at Causal IQ (Jun 2019 - Nov 2022)
- Director of Research and Technology at RE/MAX of Naperville (Sep 2014 - Jun 2019)
- Director of Operations, North America at DoveMed (Mar 2015 - Nov 2018)

## What I built at Confidential AdTech Startup
- Customer Data Platform (CDP) — 21M+ unique consumer profiles, 1B+ behavioral data points, 6 DSP integrations, activation by major DSP partner for pharmaceutical advertiser campaigns
- Two-sided AdTech platform end-to-end (consumer side + advertiser side)
- 15-person AdTech startup, $3.6M-6M ARR, 85% gross margins
- MCP-based sales prospecting workflows using LLM agents

## What I did at Causal IQ
- Managed up to $1.2M/month in programmatic spend across the client book
- Notable clients: CDC, Hertz, Grammarly, Orangetheory, Primo Water, AAA Auto, PMI Colombia, Thomas J. Henry, Party City, Floor & Decor, national political campaign teams
- Built custom CTV measurement framework — found CTV+Display reduced time-to-signup by 5-7 days vs. Display-only for Thomas J. Henry; framework handed off to Causal IQ at departure
- Grew Floor & Decor from $10K to $250K/month (25x) through pitched media recommendations
- Grew Thomas J. Henry from $700K to $1.2M/month
- Ranked #1 or #2 across 22-person account operations team

- CourtVision (courtvision.app) — NBA analytics platform built in 3 days
- Stomach-Brain Coupling Explorer — Stanford research visualization tool
